source.title: Beyond Forgetting: Representation Misdirection Elicits Controllable Side Behaviors and Capabilities
source.authors: Dang Huu-Tien; The-Hai Nguyen; Phuong Mai Dinh; P. Nguyen; A. Bui; Thanh-Tung Hoang; Le-Minh Nguyen; Naoya Inoue

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or file problem; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether attacks recover behavior suppressed by unlearning, using its own representation-misdirection methods and several recovery attacks rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own robustness experiments in Appendix F bear on recovery after unlearning. Results cited from earlier work are not recorded. It does not test weight quantization or ordinary prompt rephrasing. Some attack-table entries are flattened and their per-model values cannot be assigned confidently; the rows below use the paper’s explicit prose results instead.
record.test_reason: Appendix F runs knowledge-recovery attacks (Logitlens, LoRA fine-tuning, orthogonalization, Enhanced GCG, pruning; following Łucki et al.) on the authors' RAd/RAb unlearned Zephyr-7B models on WMDP. Tables 15–16 and Figures 12–13 report WMDP accuracy under attack. The main paper is about concept-driven side behaviours, but these results bear directly on whether the unlearning resists recovery. This is a different unlearning method from the originals aimed at the same question, and the study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong. The paper's main conclusion is that RM unlearning with a concept target vector elicits controllable side behaviours. On robustness (App. F), the authors find RAd/RAb models vulnerable to recovery regardless of concept direction: parameter-modifying attacks often restore near-base accuracy, while Logitlens and Enhanced GCG are generally less effective. They also find that unrelated Wikitext fine-tuning fails, and they concede the methods may be superficial masking. Their caveat about not establishing reliability across models concerns concept controllability, not recovery.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and tests RAd/RAb representation-misdirection variants using concept directions; it does not replicate GA, Who’s Harry Potter, or the original WMDP unlearning recipe in its recovery tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery depends on the fine-tuning data: forget and forget-relevant samples recover knowledge, whereas unrelated Wikitext does not. Enhanced GCG is less effective than attacks that modify parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: RAd/RAb with concept target vectors induce or suppress truthfulness, sentiment, refusal, bias, language and ICL behaviours while unlearning WMDP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-misdirection unlearning has controllable side effects set by the choice of target vector.

record.problems: Robustness evidence is on the paper’s RAd/RAb models, not attacks against the compared GA and other baselines. Several attack-table values cannot be reliably assigned from the flattened text. Exact small-sample recovery thresholds are not stated in the prose, and no quantization or ordinary prompt-rephrasing tests are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 15–16 contain model- and attack-specific values, but their flattened layout in the supplied text does not support reliable assignment of every value to a model and attack. These are not transcribed as separate numeric rows; the explicit aggregate findings from F.3 are recorded instead.

untested.parts: Robustness of GA, NPO, DPO, SimNPO, RMU or WHP under attack is not tested; attacks target only RAd/RAb.
No exact minimal sample count is stated in prose. Recovery from unrelated data fails rather than being shown.
No probing or weight analysis shows that the knowledge persists; the only internal evidence is recovery by direction ablation, pruning and Logitlens.
Quantization of unlearned weights is not tested.
Ordinary rephrasing, other languages, in-context information and hand-written jailbreaks are not tested; only Enhanced GCG.
No newer robust counter-method is evaluated against the attacks.

missing.what: Per-model accuracy-under-attack values are readable and should be rows. Example: WMDP-Bio fine-tuning with 5 forget samples gives RAd 59.0/25.3/29.1/44.8 and RAb 62.9/63.8/58.1/61.5 (random/truth/sentiment/refusal).
Pruning attack (set-difference SNIP) result. RAd WMDP-Bio 57.2/56.1/49.9/47.6 vs base 63.9, with MMLU largely kept. This is an internal weight edit that recovers knowledge.
Logitlens readout. RAd stays at chance at all layers, but RAb models are vulnerable at middle layers, suggesting access is blocked rather than knowledge deleted for RAb.
Cross-domain recovery. Attacks with Bio data also restore Cyber accuracy, e.g. orthogonalization gives RAd WMDP-Cyber about 40–42 vs base 43.3.
Pre-attack unlearning effectiveness. RAd brings WMDP to about 25–30 (near chance) with MMLU about 52–56 vs 58.4. RAb-random fails to unlearn (60.5), so its 'recovery' rows are not recovery.

record.verdict_notes: All recovery evidence comes from Zephyr-7B RAd/RAb models, inferred from the table hyperparameter context; the model is not stated in Tables 15–16. Attacks are white-box and some need the base model (orthogonalization). The reader's claim that the tables are flattened and unreadable is mistaken; the values align with columns.

versions.untested_parts: Recovery attacks are evaluated on this paper’s RAd/RAb models, not as robustness tests of GA, Who’s Harry Potter, or the other listed methods. Its own methods’ attack robustness is tested, but simple paraphrasing and quantization are not.
The study evaluates forget-set and closely related examples, and Wikitext as an unrelated dataset; it does not establish a specific minimum number of examples that restores knowledge.

The orthogonalization attack removes a difference-in-mean unlearning direction, not a separately identified concept activation direction. The paper discusses masking versus erasure but does not establish that all targeted knowledge remains in weights.
The tested prompt attack is Enhanced GCG’s optimized adversarial prefix. Ordinary rephrasing, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
The paper does not test a newer counter-method specifically designed to resist the listed recovery attacks.

rows.check: Version ids 'V1, V2' are invalid; use A, B. Prose (F.3, Fig. 13) says full recovery with a small number of forget samples.
